pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Acute Intermittent Porphyria (AIP) THE SMOKING GUN: Dark reddish-amber urine negative for red blood cells (porphobilinogen/porphyrins turning dark on light exposure) and acute iatrogenic collapse following the administration of a potent CYP450 inducer (Phenytoin), which drastically accelerated porphyrin accumulation. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: AIP is an autosomal dominant metabolic disorder caused by a deficiency in hydroxymethylbilane synthase (porphobilinogen deaminase) in the heme biosynthesis pathway. When triggered by fasting, stress, or CYP-inducing drugs (like phenytoin), hepatic ALAS1 is markedly upregulated, leading to the massive overproduction and accumulation of neurotoxic heme intermediates—namely delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) and porphobilinogen (PBG). These neurotoxins cause widespread autonomic dysregulation (severe abdominal pain, hypertension, tachycardia), central nervous system dysfunction (psychosis, seizures, SIADH-induced hyponatremia), and profound peripheral motor axonopathy resulting in ascending flaccid paralysis.
